# TruffleHog path exclusions for the Security workflow.
#
# One RE2 regex per line, matched against the repository-relative file path.
# Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored by TruffleHog.
#
# ONLY add a path here when the credential it matches is a placeholder or a
# local-development-only value that grants no access to anything real. These
# exclusions apply to the whole of git history, so a path listed here is a
# blind spot forever after - prefer fixing the file over adding to this list.
#
# The Security workflow scans full history on its scheduled run, so rewriting
# or deleting a file does NOT clear a finding: the old blob is still reachable
# from old commits. That is why the paths below are matched rather than the
# offending files simply being cleaned up.
#
# NOTE: do not paste example connection strings into this file. TruffleHog
# scans it like any other file, and a credential-shaped comment here becomes a
# permanent self-inflicted finding.

# Local-only Docker Compose database credentials. These services bind to
# localhost on a developer machine or an ephemeral CI runner and are never
# reachable from anywhere else.
# `infra/compose/` is the current home; the repo-root paths are where these
# files lived before they were moved, and remain reachable in history.
^docker-compose\.ya?ml$
^docker-compose\.ci\.ya?ml$
^infra/compose/docker-compose\.ya?ml$
^infra/compose/docker-compose\.ci\.ya?ml$

# Agent instruction docs. Both carry an illustrative placeholder database URL
# (literal `user` / `pass` against a literal `host`) in the environment
# variable examples. `claude.md` is the pre-rename path of `CLAUDE.md` and
# survives in history.
^AGENTS\.md$
^[Cc][Ll][Aa][Uu][Dd][Ee]\.md$
